beats.narration_slice: In 1900, sponge divers found a wreck off Antikythera.
beats.visual: Vertical technical-drawing scene of two sponge divers descending toward a broken ancient shipwreck on the rocky seabed, scattered amphorae emerging from deep Aegean blue beneath them, all framed by the recurring patinated-bronze instrument bezel.
beats.purpose: show the discovery of the Antikythera shipwreck by sponge divers
beats.visual_fingerprint: wide underwater establishing view; two descending divers above a wreck and amphora field; high three-quarter angle; deep blue seafloor setting; cool raking light with faint ochre highlights; composition led diagonally from divers to wreck
beats.continuity: opens the archaeological subject world at the wreck site

beats.narration_slice: Its cargo included a corroded bronze lump.
beats.visual: Close archaeological technical drawing of a rough green-brown bronze fragment lying among broken amphora shards and seabed sediment, isolated as the clear focal object inside the vellum illustration window.
beats.purpose: identify the unremarkable-looking corroded bronze object recovered from the wreck
beats.visual_fingerprint: tight artifact close-up; single irregular verdigris bronze lump half-buried among pottery fragments; low seabed-level angle; shallow wreck-debris zone; stronger warm bronze glint; centered asymmetrical composition
beats.continuity: moves from the wreck as a whole to one specific piece of recovered cargo

beats.narration_slice: Inside were tightly packed, precision-cut gears.
beats.visual: Cutaway technical illustration of the corroded fragment opened visually to reveal a dense cluster of intermeshing bronze gear wheels, with precise compass-drawn teeth and restrained engraving hatching but no labels.
beats.purpose: reveal that the corroded fragment contained a compact system of precision-cut gears
beats.visual_fingerprint: macro cutaway reconstruction; overlapping interlocking gear train exposed inside broken bronze casing; straight-on sectional view; neutral vellum field rather than seabed; pale celestial-blue edge accents; dense circular composition concentrated in the upper-middle
beats.continuity: reveals the mechanical interior of the bronze fragment shown in the previous beat

beats.narration_slice: The mechanism was built over two thousand years ago.
beats.visual: A restrained historical technical drawing places a reconstructed bronze mechanism on a Hellenistic workbench beside a hand compass, bronze filings and an oil lamp silhouette, with an abstract worn celestial motif behind it and no readable markings.
beats.purpose: establish that the geared instrument belongs to the Hellenistic Greek world more than two millennia ago
beats.visual_fingerprint: medium workshop tableau; reconstructed mechanism resting beside period hand tools; side-on eye-level angle; Hellenistic craft setting; warmer lamp-like bronze glints against parchment cream; mechanism offset right with tools forming a triangular composition
beats.continuity: shifts from internal construction to the ancient context in which the instrument was made

beats.narration_slice: A hand crank moved pointers across astronomical dials.
beats.visual: Oblique technical reconstruction showing a human hand turning a small side crank while linked gears drive slender bronze pointers around concentric astronomical dials, with motion implied by fine arc lines rather than modern graphics.
beats.purpose: show how hand power drove the mechanism's pointers across its dials
beats.visual_fingerprint: three-quarter mechanical action view; hand operating crank while pointers sweep concentric dial faces; elevated oblique angle; isolated instrument demonstration on vellum; cool light with focused bronze highlights; strong left-to-right action from crank to pointer tips
beats.continuity: moves from the ancient object's context to a clear demonstration of its manual operation

beats.narration_slice: One dial tracked the Sun and Moon.
beats.visual: Front-facing technical drawing of a single circular dial with two distinct pointer markers represented by a small sun disk and moon sphere, arranged against restrained orbital geometry with no letters or numerals.
beats.purpose: show that one dial represented the positions or cycles of the Sun and Moon
beats.visual_fingerprint: clean frontal dial study; paired sun-disk and moon-sphere indicators on one circular face; orthographic angle; abstract celestial vellum setting; sparse pale-blue orbital accents; balanced concentric composition with large negative space around the dial
beats.continuity: isolates one function from the broader moving-dial mechanism

beats.narration_slice: Others modeled cycles used to predict eclipses.
beats.visual: A vertical eclipse-cycle diagram rendered as nested bronze-and-charcoal orbital rings, with repeated moon positions culminating in a darkened Sun-Moon alignment, visually linked to a small gear segment below and containing no symbols that resemble readable text.
beats.purpose: explain that additional geared cycles could indicate repeating patterns associated with eclipses
beats.visual_fingerprint: abstract celestial cycle diagram; sequence of moon positions around nested rings ending in eclipse alignment; top-down geometric view; diagrammatic sky field; stronger charcoal shadow at eclipse point; sweeping spiral composition descending toward a small gear segment
beats.continuity: expands from the simple Sun-and-Moon dial to a more complex repeating astronomical cycle

beats.narration_slice: Another tracked the cycle of major Greek games.
beats.visual: Technical-drawing interpretation of a separate circular cycle dial paired with a small engraved-style olive wreath, stadium turning post and runner silhouette as non-textual visual cues for recurring Greek games.
beats.purpose: show that the mechanism also tracked the repeating schedule of major Greek athletic games
beats.visual_fingerprint: medium symbolic dial composition; separate cycle wheel accompanied by olive wreath and tiny runner motif; slight low angle; parchment-and-bronze civic festival setting; muted ochre accents replacing celestial blue; dial anchored lower-left with game symbols rising upper-right
beats.continuity: shifts from astronomical cycles to a distinct calendrical cycle connected with Greek games

beats.narration_slice: Inscriptions even explained parts of its operation.
beats.visual: Extreme close technical drawing of a surviving bronze plate surface covered in shallow, fragmentary inscription-like incisions rendered only as illegible archaeological texture, beside the edge of a gear and pointer to suggest operating instructions without readable generated text.
beats.purpose: show that engraved inscriptions on the mechanism provided explanatory information about its operation
beats.visual_fingerprint: extreme archaeological surface close-up; worn bronze plate with dense non-readable incised texture beside partial gear teeth and pointer tip; raking side angle; fragment-study setting; strongest cool grazing light emphasizing scratches; cropped composition dominated by patinated surface texture
beats.continuity: ends on physical evidence from the artifact itself after showing its major modeled cycles
